subject: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment options for Crescent Biomed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@crescentbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment options for Crescent Biomed

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call highlights:
- Crescent Biomed is evaluating private deployment (VPC or on-prem) due to PHI handling and upcoming clinical integrations.
- Compliance: SOC 2 and HIPAA are primary asks; GDPR applicability for EEA data.
- Network: you prefer minimal public egress and are evaluating an air-gapped/isolated topology for sensitive workloads.

Requested by Crescent during the call:
- Vendor security questionnaire (we said we could start it)
- High level network diagram showing options we support (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, private control plane, & air-gapped patterns)
- Evidence list: SOC 2 report, data retention & logging controls, KMS/HSM integration options

What I'll do: attach our Private Deployment checklist and a template network diagram as a starting point. Lauren from Solutions will coordinate the technical deep-dive and have an engineer fill the questionnaire with you.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) I’ll send the questionnaire to you to capture Crescent-specific items (today).
2) Lauren to schedule a 60-min technical session next week to walk through topology and integration questions.
3) We’ll produce a preliminary network diagram and a short evidence pack (SOC 2 guidance + logging/retention notes) within 4 business days after the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.pdf

Wanted to flag two items that typically come up so you can prep: BYOK/KMS requirements (we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations) and any procurement timelines for an on-prem trial or VPC peering approvals.

If this looks right, I’ll kick off the questionnaire and loop Lauren.

— Ben
Director, Strategic Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@crescentbio.com>

Cc: Priya Kumar <pkumar@crescentbio.com>; Michael Orton <michael.orton@crescentbio.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment options for Crescent Biomed

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few updates and answers from our side, plus an initial questionnaire attached.

Compliance status:
- SOC 2: Type I completed Q4 2027; Type II in progress with audit window May–Jul 2028 (expected report Aug 2028).
- HIPAA: We are a covered entity with internal BAAs in place with several vendors; vendor-specific BAAs will be required for any PHI-processing endpoints.
- GDPR: We process some EEA data; data residency and DPIA will be relevant for EU workloads.

Network constraints and asks:
- Primary preference: VPC peering (private connectivity) with no public-facing endpoints for inference traffic.
- Alternative: Transit Gateway / PrivateLink approach if peering is not possible at scale.
- Air-gapped option: We have an internal engineering team that can accept an air-gapped bundle for an on-prem install if absolutely required — question is around automated updates and patching.

Attached for your team: crescent-vendor-sec-questionnaire.xlsx — this includes both security questionnaire and a short inventory of compliance evidence we need. Priya (cc’d) will own the questionnaire from our side.

Outstanding items for Redwood to confirm (can be handled in the technical deep-dive):
- Example network topologies (VPC-peering / Transit GW / fully air-gapped) and where the control plane resides in each case.
- How customer-managed KMS / HSM is supported (BYOK flow, key rotation, audit logs).
- Logging retention and sampling for token-level logs (retention windows + redaction options).
- Expected SLAs & fallbacks for private deployments (failover to hosted vs queued requests).

If you can send the questionnaire and the sample topology before the deep-dive, that will help us prep. Looking at availability — Priya and I can do 60 minutes on Tuesday 5/23 or Wednesday 5/24 (PDT).

Thanks — Alex
Head of IT Security, Crescent Biomed

Subject: Re: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment options for Crescent Biomed

Alex / Priya — looping in from Solutions to capture the technical asks and propose an approach. Short answers and proposed plan below.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Network topologies: we support three canonical patterns:
  1) VPC peering (private subnets for inference; control plane access via customer-managed VPC endpoint; no public egress required).
  2) Transit Gateway / PrivateLink (recommended at scale for multi-VPC architectures).
  3) Air-gapped on-prem bundle (off-line installer, manual patch cadence; patching policy and signing provided).
- Control plane: private control plane option keeps management plane in your VPC or transits over private endpoints — no public management endpoints exposed.
- KMS / HSM: BYOK supported via standard KMS APIs and we have partners for HSM integrations. We can provide an architecture note and TOC for evidence.
- Logging/retention: token-level cost/latency logs can be retained per your retention policy; redaction options exist for PHI (we also support field-level redaction).
- SLA/fallbacks: for Dedicated and Private we provide explicit throughput SLOs; for air-gapped we’ll define a local support/patch cadence and a manual failover plan.

Proposed immediate next steps (technical track):
1) Ben will share our Private Deployment checklist and a preliminary network diagram (done).
2) We propose a 60-min technical deep-dive on Tue 2028-05-23 at 10:00 PDT to review the crescent questionnaire and map out a topology. Please confirm.
3) After the deep-dive we’ll produce: a) a tailored network diagram for Crescent, b) a filled questionnaire draft for your review, c) an evidence pack with SOC 2 guidance and KMS/HSM options (target: 4 business days).

I attached a small sample network diagram and a short response template to help Priya and your procurement team. If the air-gapped path is a hard requirement we’ll include a patch/update cadence and signing metadata in the evidence pack.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-sample.pdf

Action owners:
- Lauren: run the deep-dive and produce diagram + evidence pack (owner)
- Ben: procurement coordination and timeline (owner)
- Priya: complete questionnaire and identify any additional compliance asks from legal/procurement

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
